caption: A man pushes a broken-down car along a flat empty street, and the car slowly starts to roll.

sa.check: A man pushes a car along a flat street.
The street is flat and empty.
The push comes first and the roll follows.

pc.expect: The car begins to move only after he pushes and only while he pushes, and it gathers speed slowly.
pc.fail: The car moves before he touches it; or rolls with his hands off it; or surges away fast from a push.

pc.expect: He leans forward with his arms against the car and drives with his legs, and his limbs bend at the joints.
pc.fail: His arms bend mid-forearm; or a limb detaches; or his hands pass through the car.

pc.expect: His hands are on the car body and his feet on the road.
pc.fail: His hands pass through the car; or he passes into the car; or his feet sink into the road.

pc.expect: The car rolls in the direction he pushes, in a straight line.
pc.fail: It rolls toward him; or turns sharply on its own; or rolls backward.

pc.expect: His limbs keep their number, and one car stays one car.
pc.fail: A limb detaches; or the car duplicates; or he merges with the car.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: His clothing, the car and the street stay the same.
pc.fail: His clothing changes colour; or the car changes colour; or the street rearranges.

note: Biomechanics scene: the body is the physics. Gait, posture, style and skill are not judged; only that limbs stay attached, bend at joints, keep ground contact and pass through nothing.
